articles.title: One-Year Outcomes of Surgical Versus Endovascular Revascularization for Acute Limb Ischemia in the SAPLING-ALI Registry.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Despite the increasing use of endovascular therapy as an alternative to surgery for acute limb ischemia, individualized treatment selection remains challenging. We compared outcomes of endovascular therapy versus surgery and sought to identify patient characteristics favoring either strategy.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included consecutive patients with acute limb ischemia (Rutherford category 1-2b) who underwent revascularization at 13 Japanese institutions between July 2011 and March 2025; patients with thrombosed popliteal artery aneurysm were excluded. The primary outcome was amputation-free survival, defined as freedom from major amputation or death from any cause. The primary analysis was a Cox model adjusted for 13 baseline covariates with hospital as a categorical covariate; propensity score weighting was used as a sensitivity analysis. Subgroup analyses were performed to identify characteristics favoring either strategy.

RESULTS: Of 978 patients (endovascular therapy, n = 607; surgery, n = 371), those treated with endovascular therapy more often had diabetes, hemodialysis, dementia, and non-ambulatory status. Unadjusted 1-year amputation-free survival was lower with endovascular therapy than with surgery (68.7% vs 76.3%; log-rank P = .001), but the adjusted hazard ratio for death or major amputation was 1.03 (95% confidence interval, 0.77-1.38; P = .84). Results were consistent with overlap weighting (hazard ratio 1.15; 95% confidence interval, 0.93-1.42) and across other sensitivity analyses. Thirty-day mortality was 13.1% after endovascular therapy and 8.9% after surgery (P = .05), and the difference was attenuated after weighting. No subgroup favoring either strategy was identified (all P for interaction ≥ .18).

CONCLUSIONS: Unadjusted amputation-free survival was lower after endovascular therapy than after surgery, but the difference disappeared after adjustment for patient characteristics and hospital, and no subgroup favoring either strategy was identified. Endovascular therapy, being less invasive, may be a reasonable alternative to surgery for acute limb ischemia.

articles.title: Longitudinal Trends of Intact and Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repairs in the United States: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted access to elective procedures and routine care. Given the risk of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture, understanding repair trends is important to assess the impact of the pandemic on vascular outcomes.

METHODS: This repeated cross-sectional analysis used the TriNetX network, a multicenter US electronic health records database. We included 423 874 patients diagnosed with AAA from 2016 to 2024. Patients were categorized by clinical presentation-intact AAA and ruptured AAA-and stratified by surgical approach: endovascular aneurysm repair or open aneurysm repair. Annual trends in AAA repair rates were assessed using joinpoint regression to calculate annual percentage change.

RESULTS: Among 19 330 AAA repairs, 3791 (19.6%) were open aneurysm repair, and 15 539 (80.4%) were endovascular aneurysm repair. From 2018 to 2024, 1623 repairs (9.9%) were for ruptured AAA and 14 835 (90.1%) were for intact AAA. The rate of intact AAA repairs initially remained stable from 2018 to 2022 but significantly decreased after the pandemic from 2022 to 2024 (annual percentage change, -2.87% [95% CI, -10.95 to -1.00]). In contrast, ruptured AAA repairs rates shifted sharply during the pandemic, with an established prepandemic decline in ruptured repairs from 2018 to 2020 (annual percentage change, -11.48%) reversed, with an increase from 2020 to 2022 (annual percentage change +12.01%), before declining from 2022 to 2024 (annual percentage change, -11.00%).

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, repairs for intact AAA declined, while repairs for ruptured AAA increased during the pandemic period. These trends suggest that potential delays in routine surveillance and elective surgery during the pandemic may have increased acute presentations.

Given the risk of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture, understanding repair trends is important to assess the impact of the pandemic on vascular outcomes. METHODS: This repeated cross-sectional analysis used the TriNetX network, a multicenter US electronic health records database.

articles.title: Predicting Morbidity, Mortality, Revision, and Ambulation in Patients Undergoing Major Lower Limb Amputation for Peripheral Arterial Disease or Diabetes Mellitus: The Case for Regional Level Clinical Prediction Models.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Several outcome prediction tools exist to support decision making for patients undergoing major lower limb amputation (MLLA). However, most predict a single outcome, are derived from registry level data, and lack external validation. The present study aimed to develop clinically focussed, multi-outcome prediction tools using granular regional data with immediate external validation on an international database.

METHODS: This study involved development, and internal and external validation of multivariable binomial and multinomial regression prediction models. All patients undergoing MLLA for ischaemic or diabetic indications between 1 January 2013 and 1 July 2023 at a single regional vascular hub were used for model development. Clinically focussed logistic multivariable binomial and multinomial regression models were developed predicting 30 day and 1 year mortality and revision, 30 day major morbidity or mortality, and best mobility achieved (binary and 3 category). Model complexity, crossvalidated receiver operating curve (ROC) discrimination and calibration were assessed and optimised, with the best performing models undergoing external validation on PERCEIVE study data. External validity was assessed using discrimination and calibration statistics, with one revision attempt permitted.

RESULTS: The development dataset included 609 patients (75.2% men, median age 69 years). Internal crossvalidated ROC values were 0.774 for 30 day mortality, 0.752 for 1 year mortality, 0.679 for 30 day revision, 0.707 for 1 year revision, 0.699 for 30 day major morbidity or mortality, 0.876 for binary best ambulation, and 0.752 for 3 category best ambulation predictions. All models were well calibrated. On external validation the ROC values were 0.616, 0.722, 0.617, 0.488, 0.697, 0.643, and 0.602, respectively.

CONCLUSION: The prediction models performed well for internal "regional" patient outcomes, especially for mortality and ambulation. On external validation, like other models externally validated on the PERCEIVE data, they failed to generalise to the wider population undergoing MLLA, except for 1 year mortality. Predicting patient outcomes from pre-operative variables remains challenging; however, regional level modelling may provide better performance over more general prediction tools.

articles.title: Predictors of Clinically Meaningful 1-Year Health Status Improvements Following Endovascular or Surgical Revascularization: Insights From the BEST-CLI Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite efforts to promote limb salvage in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), the factors associated with meaningful health status improvement after revascularization remain poorly understood. We examined predictors of meaningful 1-year health status improvement following revascularization for CLTI.

METHODS: We pooled endovascular and surgical arms from the BEST-CLI (Best Endovascular Versus Best Surgical Therapy in Patients With CLTI) randomized controlled trial, including patients with CLTI (150 international sites, 2014-2019). Health status was assessed at baseline and 1 year using the peripheral artery disease-specific Vascular Quality of Life questionnaire, the generic European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, and the Short Form-12 Physical and Mental Component Summary. Distribution-based minimal clinically important difference thresholds were defined as 0.5 SD of baseline health status scores. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of no meaningful 1-year improvement (same/worsened versus improved).

RESULTS: Among 1017 patients (72.0% men, mean age 66.8±9.7 years), clinically meaningful improvements were reported by 76.5% for Vascular Quality of Life, 52.8% European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, 56.7% for Short Form-12 Physical Component Summary, and 42.1% for Short Form-12 Mental Component Summary, regardless of revascularization type (surgical versus endovascular). Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status increased the odds of no meaningful improvement. Revascularization type was not associated with Vascular Quality of Life improvement (odds ratio, 1.059 [95% CI, 0.91-1.23]; P=0.445; C statistic=0.77).

CONCLUSIONS: One-year postrevascularization, over three-fourths of individuals with CLTI perceived meaningful improvements in peripheral artery disease-specific health, and over half improved overall physical health, regardless of procedure type. Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status predicted 1-year health status response. REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02060630.

articles.title: Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Studies comparing aspirin with anticoagulants for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty have had conflicting results.

METHODS: In a comparative-effectiveness noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned patients undergoing elective hip or knee arthroplasty to receive aspirin (81 mg twice daily), warfarin (to a target international normalized ratio of 2.0), or rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) for 30 days. The composite primary effectiveness outcome (death from any cause or symptomatic VTE) and primary safety outcome (bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or myocardial infarction) were evaluated through 6 months in a blinded fashion. The noninferiority margin for the risk difference was 0.69 percentage points.

RESULTS: Among 18,883 participants who had undergone randomization, 15,317 (7214 with hip arthroplasty and 8103 with knee arthroplasty) were included in the primary per-protocol analysis. A primary effectiveness outcome event occurred in 77 of 6090 participants (1.26%) in the aspirin group, in 52 of 4231 (1.23%) in the warfarin group, and in 47 of 4996 (0.94%) in the rivaroxaban group; a primary safety outcome event occurred in 177 (2.91%), 142 (3.36%), and 174 (3.48%), respectively. In pairwise comparisons, 6-month risks of a primary effectiveness outcome event were 1.24% and 0.94% for aspirin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.30 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.20 to 0.81); 1.24% and 1.01% for aspirin versus warfarin (difference, 0.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.34 to 0.81); and 1.13% and 1.10% for warfarin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.57 to 0.63). Risks of a primary safety outcome event were 3.70% and 3.02% for rivaroxaban versus aspirin (difference, 0.68 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.41); 3.65% and 2.88% for warfarin versus aspirin (difference, 0.77 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.58); and 3.59% and 3.61% for rivaroxaban versus warfarin (difference, -0.02 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.89 to 0.85). Intention-to-treat analyses yielded similar results.

CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty was not noninferior to rivaroxaban or warfarin with respect to death or symptomatic VTE. Warfarin and rivaroxaban were not noninferior to aspirin for safety. (Funded by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute; PEPPER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT02810704.).

articles.title: Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative Contemporary Benchmarks: Thoracic Endovascular Aortic Repair.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe contemporary outcomes as well as temporal trends of in-hospital mortality and complication rates for patients undergoing thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) across indications and levels of urgency, establishing a benchmark for future analytic efforts.

METHODS: The VQI TEVAR and complex EVAR registry was queried for procedures performed between January 2014-December 2024. Primary outcomes included in-hospital mortality and major complications. Analyses were stratified by indication to include descending thoracic aortic aneurysms (DTAA), dissections, and trauma. Aneurysms involving the aortic arch (i.e. landing zone < 2) or extending to the visceral segment and distally (i.e. landing zone >5) were excluded. Linear regression and the Cochran Armitage test for trend were used to analyze yearly mortality and complication rates over time. Mortality and complication end-points were further analyzed using logistic regression with and without risk-adjustment.

RESULTS: Over the ten-year study period, 4,632 TEVARs were performed for DTAA, 6,701 for dissection, and 2,321 for trauma. For patients undergoing TEVAR for DTAA, in-hospital mortality declined significantly for both elective (2014, 3.9% versus 2024, 1.0%, -0.26 percentage points per year, p=0.01) and nonelective cases (2014, 16.7% versus 2024, 8.7%, -0.63 percentage points per year, p=0.04). There was also a decline in in-hospital mortality among elective dissection patients (2014, 3.7% versus 2024, 0.5%, -0.17 percentage points per year, p=0.03). Elective TEVAR overall is associated with a mortality rate of less than two percent per year. The in-hospital complication trends declined significantly for patients undergoing TEVAR for DTAA - elective patients experienced a decline in complication rates by -1.13 percentage points per year (2014, 24.8% versus 2024, 11.5% p<0.001) and non-elective patients experienced a decline in complication rates by -2.0 percentage points per year (2014, 40.5% versus 2024, 25.2%, p<0.001). Dissection patients undergoing elective repair had a decrease of -0.8 percentage points per year (2014, 16.9% versus 2024, 9.2%, p<0.001). Nonelective dissections repairs had a complication rate of 36.4% in 2014 vs 34.1% in 2024, p=0.874). Trauma patients tended toward higher complication rates over time, with a rate of 21.6% in 2014 and 32.2% in 2024, p=0.06) Trauma patients experienced an overall increase in in-hospital mortality of +0.38 percentage points per year (2014, 9.8% versus 2024, 9.4%, p=0.01).

CONCLUSION: Temporal trends within the VQI demonstrate improvements in mortality and complication rates for patients undergoing TEVAR for DTAA and elective dissection repair, with contemporary yearly mortality rates of less than two percent. Patients undergoing non-elective dissection repair and those with traumatic indications represent challenging and complex pathologies requiring further research to identify opportunities to improve outcomes.

articles.title: Index Below-Knee Endovascular Intervention for Intermittent Claudication Is Associated with Increased Amputation Risk.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Guidelines advise against infrapopliteal peripheral vascular intervention (PVI) for intermittent claudication (IC) due to potential harm with unclear benefit. We hypothesized that below-knee intervention at index PVI for IC confers higher future amputation risk than above-knee-only treatment.

METHODS: From the VQI PVI registry (2015-2025), we identified elective, initial PVIs for IC and compared those patients undergoing above-knee-only treatment (AK) to those having any below-knee intervention (BK). Using our previously described methodology, long-term amputation data were obtained by linking the PVI and amputation registries via unique patient identifiers. Demographic and procedural data were analyzed descriptively. Kaplan-Meier Analysis estimated risk of major and any (major+minor) amputation, with independent predictors of amputation identified by multivariable Firth logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among 92,899 treated limbs (81,338 AK; 11,561 BK), BK patients had increased rates of diabetes (54% vs. 41%), CHF (18% vs. 13%), and ESRD/dialysis (4.7% vs. 1.7%, p<0.001). BK patients were more likely to be Black (21% vs. 13%, p<0.001), Hispanic (8.8% vs. 4.3%, p<0.001), and Asian (1.5% vs. 1.0%, p<0.001). Smoking history predominated in AK (89% vs. 67%, p<0.001). 16,086 limbs required repeat PVI, 13,831 (17%) in the AK group vs. 2,255 (20%) in the BK group (p<0.001). At reintervention, BK patients were more likely to have progressed to CLTI (41% vs. 25%; p<0.001) and undergo ≥2 repeat interventions (32% vs. 27%; p<0.001). Initial below-knee intervention was associated with greater ipsilateral major (OR 2.39;1.70-3.35) and any (OR 2.36;1.75-3.18) amputation. Kaplan-Meier showed increased major [1-year (0.3% vs 0.1%);5-years (0.4% vs 0.1%)] and any amputation risk [1-year (0.5% vs 0.1%); 5-years (0.7% vs 0.2%).

CONCLUSIONS: Index below-knee intervention for IC portends greater risk of progression to CLTI, repeat PVI, and ipsilateral amputation, highlighting the potentially dangerous treatment trap of infrapopliteal intervention in patients with intermittent claudicants.

articles.title: Two-Year Outcomes of the Prospective THRILLER Registry on Popliteal and Infrapopliteal Endovascular Interventions for CLTI.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Over 70% of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) present with below-the-knee disease, and there is a growing trend towards endovascular revascularization.

OBJECTIVES: The Dutch Chronic Lower Limb-Threatening Ischemia Registry (THRILLER) aimed to provide real-world data on outcomes after popliteal and infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization to guide revascularization strategies.

METHODS: This prospective multicenter registry included consecutive CLTI patients undergoing popliteal or infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization in seven Dutch hospitals. Primary outcomes were limb salvage and amputation-free survival (AFS) at 24 months, estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method.

RESULTS: Between February 2021 and December 2023, a total of 1,119 interventions in 1,060 limbs (938 patients) were included, treating 551 popliteal, 1,352 tibial, and 239 pedal lesions. The median follow-up was 43.6 months (Q1-Q3: 35.5-52.7 months). Overall, 78.4% (831/1,060) of the limbs were Rutherford 5 and 8.1% (86/1,060) were Rutherford 6; 41.3% (382/926) were WIfI (Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection) stage 4. Technical success was achieved in 92.3% (1,033/1,119). Limb salvage and AFS decreased significantly after technical failure and with increasing WIfI stage and Rutherford category. Compared to Rutherford 5, Rutherford 6 limbs had significantly worse limb salvage (HR: 3.07; 95% CI: 1.89-4.99; P < 0.001) and AFS (HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.50-2.86; P < 0.001). For AFS, the excess risk of Rutherford 6 was greatest in the first 3 months (HR: 14.13; 95% CI: 4.94-40.38 vs Rutherford 4; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Endovascular revascularization for popliteal and infrapopliteal disease in patients with CLTI is safe and effective in preventing limb loss and mortality at 2 years, although patients with Rutherford 6 limbs face significantly worse outcomes, particularly in the first 3 months.

articles.title: One-Year Outcomes of Surgical Versus Endovascular Revascularization for Acute Limb Ischemia in the SAPLING-ALI Registry.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Despite the increasing use of endovascular therapy as an alternative to surgery for acute limb ischemia, individualized treatment selection remains challenging. We compared outcomes of endovascular therapy versus surgery and sought to identify patient characteristics favoring either strategy.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included consecutive patients with acute limb ischemia (Rutherford category 1-2b) who underwent revascularization at 13 Japanese institutions between July 2011 and March 2025; patients with thrombosed popliteal artery aneurysm were excluded. The primary outcome was amputation-free survival, defined as freedom from major amputation or death from any cause. The primary analysis was a Cox model adjusted for 13 baseline covariates with hospital as a categorical covariate; propensity score weighting was used as a sensitivity analysis. Subgroup analyses were performed to identify characteristics favoring either strategy.

RESULTS: Of 978 patients (endovascular therapy, n = 607; surgery, n = 371), those treated with endovascular therapy more often had diabetes, hemodialysis, dementia, and non-ambulatory status. Unadjusted 1-year amputation-free survival was lower with endovascular therapy than with surgery (68.7% vs 76.3%; log-rank P = .001), but the adjusted hazard ratio for death or major amputation was 1.03 (95% confidence interval, 0.77-1.38; P = .84). Results were consistent with overlap weighting (hazard ratio 1.15; 95% confidence interval, 0.93-1.42) and across other sensitivity analyses. Thirty-day mortality was 13.1% after endovascular therapy and 8.9% after surgery (P = .05), and the difference was attenuated after weighting. No subgroup favoring either strategy was identified (all P for interaction ≥ .18).

CONCLUSIONS: Unadjusted amputation-free survival was lower after endovascular therapy than after surgery, but the difference disappeared after adjustment for patient characteristics and hospital, and no subgroup favoring either strategy was identified. Endovascular therapy, being less invasive, may be a reasonable alternative to surgery for acute limb ischemia.

articles.title: Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair as a Salvage Strategy after Failed Chimney Endovascular Aortic Repair: An International Multicentre Cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chimney endovascular aortic repair (chEVAR) failures, often manifesting as late type Ia endoleaks or sac expansion, present a formidable surgical challenge. Due to the variable upward orientation of pre-existing chimney stents, fenestrated solutions are frequently technically precluded. This study aimed to evaluate the outcomes of branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) as a salvage strategy for late chEVAR failure within a multicentre international cohort.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 29 consecutive patients (median age 81.0 years, interquartile range [IQR] 66.0, 83.0) treated across 13 European centres (2013 - 2025) for failed chEVAR using branched endografts. The primary endpoints were technical success, thirty day clinical success, and procedure related complications. Secondary endpoints included overall survival, freedom from re-intervention, and target visceral vessel (TVV) patency.

RESULTS: The median interval from index chEVAR to BEVAR re-intervention was 48.5 months (IQR 30.0, 80.8). Acute urgent or emergent procedures accounted for 17% of cases (n = 5), while 31% (n = 9) underwent expedited repair for large aneurysms. Off the shelf devices were utilised in 41% of cases. A total of 106 TVVs were incorporated through branches, with a mean of 3.7 vessels per patient. Technical success was achieved in 97% (28 of 29). There was no peri-operative mortality or open surgical conversion. Significant complications included two cases (7%) of severe spinal cord ischaemia. The thirty day clinical success rate was 90%. At a median follow up of 19 months (IQR 9, 40), the Kaplan-Meier estimate for overall survival was 92% at 1 year. TVV patency was 100%, with only one renal artery re-intervention for in stent re-stenosis. Freedom from branch related re-intervention was 96% at 1 year.

CONCLUSION: Salvage of failed chEVAR using branched endografts is technically demanding but yields excellent early results. In experienced centres, BEVAR appears feasible and offers one potential salvage option in selected patients with suitable anatomy, particularly when an off the shelf solution is required.

articles.title: The IMA-PLUS Score for Predicting Type 2 Endoleak After Endovascular Repair: Development and External Validation in European and Japanese Cohorts.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Prophylactic embolisation of infrarenal branch vessels has been investigated to prevent type 2 endoleak (EL2) following endovascular repair (EVAR) of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA), but patient selection is poorly defined. In this study, a computed tomography angiography (CTA) based risk score was developed and validated to predict EL2 after EVAR.

METHODS: This multicentre, retrospective diagnostic study used prospectively collected data from the Zenith alpha for aneurysm Repair Registry (ZEPHYR) as the development cohort. Eligible patients underwent standard EVAR with pre-operative arterial phase CTA and at least one post-operative delayed phase CTA. The model was converted into a numerical score ("IMA-PLUS Score") and validated in two retrospective cohorts. Discrimination, calibration, and risk group thresholds were assessed. In validation cohorts, freedom from AAA expansion and EL2 associated reinterventions up to 5 years were analysed.

RESULTS: Data from 245 patients of the ZEPHYR registry were included. EL2 occurred in 96 patients (39.2%). The IMA-PLUS Score includes inferior mesenteric artery diameter, number of infrarenal renal pole arteries, number of patent lumbar arteries, and median sacral artery patency, achieving a crossvalidated area under the curve (AUC) of 0.78. Using prespecified thresholds (low < 128, medium 128 - 200, high > 200), observed EL2 incidences in ZEPHYR were 19%, 59%, and 74%. In the Heidelberg cohort (n = 134; EL2 44%), AUC was 0.77 (95% confidence intervals [CI] 0.69 - 0.85) with EL2 incidences of 24%, 60%, and 89% across risk groups with good calibration; interobserver agreement for total score was high (intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.95). In the Tokyo cohort (n = 123; EL2 52.8%) AUC was 0.75 (95% CI 0.67 - 0.84); EL2 incidences were 36%, 76%, and 80%, with higher observed incidence than predicted. In validation cohorts, the IMA-PLUS Score was associated with AAA expansion and reduced freedom from EL2 associated reinterventions.

CONCLUSION: The IMA-PLUS Score may support selection of patients for future studies on preventive management strategies.

articles.title: Mortality Following Recurrent Venous Thromboembolism and Major Bleeding Stratified by Active Cancer Status.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) and major bleeding are serious complications after acute VTE. However, their independent impact on subsequent mortality in the era of direct oral anticoagulants remains unclear, particularly with respect to differences between patients with and without active cancer.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the associations of recurrent VTE and major bleeding with subsequent mortality in the overall cohort and subgroups stratified by active cancer.

METHODS: We analyzed 5,197 patients with VTE from the COMMAND VTE Registry-2 using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models with recurrent VTE and major bleeding as time-updated covariates.

RESULTS: In the overall cohort, 283 patients developed recurrent VTE, 470 developed major bleeding, and 1,323 died. Recurrent VTE and major bleeding were associated with mortality (adjusted HR: 1.65, 95% CI: 1.28-2.12, P < 0.001; adjusted HR: 3.33, 95% CI: 2.83-3.91, P < 0.001, respectively). Among patients with active cancer, both recurrent VTE and major bleeding were associated with mortality (adjusted HR: 1.95, 95% CI: 1.45-2.62, P < 0.001; adjusted HR: 2.96, 95% CI: 2.42-3.61, P < 0.001, respectively). Among patients without active cancer, only major bleeding was associated with mortality (adjusted HR: 3.78, 95% CI: 2.88-4.97, P < 0.001), whereas recurrent VTE was not associated with mortality (adjusted HR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.55-1.56, P = 0.78).

CONCLUSIONS: In contemporary real-world patients with VTE in the era of direct oral anticoagulants, major bleeding was associated with increased subsequent mortality in both patients with and without active cancer, whereas recurrent VTE was associated with increased mortality in patients with active cancer, with no significant association observed in those without active cancer.

articles.title: Zero Iodine Contrast Endovascular Aortic Repair Using Carbon Dioxide Angiography is Associated with Lower Rates of Renal Deterioration: A Multicentre, Prospective, Propensity Matched Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This prospective, multicentre, non-randomised, observational cohort study evaluated the association between a carbon dioxide (CO2) only angiography strategy during endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) and midterm renal outcomes compared with procedures requiring adjunctive iodinated contrast media (ICM).

METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing EVAR with a standardised CO2 only protocol were included. Patients were stratified according to intra-operative contrast use (CO2 only vs. CO2 + ICM). The primary endpoint was renal deterioration, defined as a persistent increase of one or more chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage(s) confirmed on two consecutive follow up assessments. Secondary endpoints included mortality, re-intervention, and aneurysm related outcomes. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to adjust for baseline differences. Multivariable regression and time to event analyses were conducted.

RESULTS: Of 291 patients (median age 78 years), 239 (82%) underwent CO2 only EVAR and 52 (18%) required adjunctive ICM. At midterm follow up (up to 24 months; mean follow up 18 months), renal deterioration was less frequent in the CO2 only group than in the CO2 + ICM group (5% vs. 23%; p < .001). Patients treated with CO2 only angiography had a significantly lower serum creatinine and higher estimated glomerular filtration rate at follow up (p < .001 for both). These findings were confirmed after PSM, with renal deterioration occurring in 6% vs. 23% of patients (p = .023). In the matched cohort, CO2 only angiography remained independently associated with lower odds of CKD stage progression (odds ratio 0.14, 95% confidence interval 0.03 - 0.45; p < .001). Thirty day and midterm mortality and endoleak rates were similar between groups, whereas re-interventions were more frequent in the CO2 + ICM group.

CONCLUSION: A zero iodine contrast, CO2 only angiography strategy during EVAR was associated with a lower rate of renal deterioration. Because patients requiring adjunctive ICM were identified intra-operatively rather than randomly allocated, residual confounding by indication cannot be excluded, despite propensity score matching. These findings support the feasibility of a CO2 first strategy and justify confirmation in randomised studies.

articles.title: Development of a machine learning model to predict venous thromboembolism risk in women using combined oral contraceptives.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality, with combined oral contraceptives (COCPs) being a modifiable risk factor. Existing clinical tools have limited ability to capture complex predictor interactions. This study aimed to develop and evaluate machine learning (ML) models to predict VTE risk among COCP users.

METHODS: This study was conducted using data from the Saudi Real-World Evidence Network (2016–2023). The primary outcome was the first VTE event within 2 years of COCP initiation. Following data partitioning, feature selection was performed on the training set. Elastic-net logistic regression, random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), one-class support vector machine and Isolation-Forest were trained on original and resampled datasets. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and F1 score.

RESULTS: The cohort included 24 518 treatment episodes (n=17 512, VTE events=52). After handling class imbalance, RF and XGBoost were the best-performing models (F1: 84.3% and 81.6%; AUROC: 59.6% and 69.2%, respectively), compared with other models (F1: 2.6%–55.3%, AUROC: 54.2%–68.4%). Key predictors included age, glucocorticoid use and rheumatic, renal and thyroid diseases.

DISCUSSION: ML shows potential for VTE risk detection despite low event rate and class imbalance. However, findings suggest synthetic sample overfitting, and external validation is warranted before clinical deployment. Identified predictors reinforce the role of metabolic and inflammatory factors in VTE susceptibility among COCP users.

CONCLUSION: ML models, particularly XGBoost and RF, demonstrated moderate predictive ability for VTE among COCP users, supporting their use in individualised risk assessments, though external validation is warranted.

Existing clinical tools have limited ability to capture complex predictor interactions. This study aimed to develop and evaluate machine learning (ML) models to predict VTE risk among COCP users.

articles.title: Machine-learning-derived laboratory signatures associated with postoperative day-3 ultrasound-detected lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis after fractures around the knee.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to construct risk-discrimination models for postoperative-day-3 ultrasound-detected lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) status in patients with fractures around the knee (FAK) using five machine-learning algorithms and compare model performance across five machine-learning algorithms.

METHODS: Electronic medical records of 1,071 patients who underwent surgical treatment for FAK at Suining Central Hospital from January 2023 to August 2026 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 749) and a test set (n = 322) at a 7:3 ratio. Feature selection occurred exclusively within the training dataset. Predictive variables were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, the Boruta algorithm, and recursive feature elimination-extreme gradient boosting (RFE-XGBoost). Five predictive models were developed, including logistic regression, k-nearest neighbor (KNN), random forest (RF), light gradient-boosting machine (LightGBM), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). Model performance was evaluated comprehensively via the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score. Receiver-operating-characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision-curve analysis (DCA) were utilized to identify the selected model. Finally, Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were employed to interpret the global and local prediction outputs of the selected model.

RESULTS: Seventeen overlapping features were identified via feature-selection procedures for final modelling, among which postoperative-day-1 and postoperative-day-3 laboratory biomarkers contributed most substantially to model output. XGBoost was chosen for subsequent SHAP interpretability analyses based on balanced performance observed in cross-validated out-of-fold outputs from the training set. Several non-linear models yielded comparably high discrimination, with overlapping 95% confidence intervals for AUROC.The cross-validated AUC for the XGBoost model in the training set was 0.9932, with a classification threshold of 0.57 derived from the Youden index. In the test set, the AUROC was 0.998 (95% CI: 0.993-1.000), AUPRC was 0.996 (95% CI: 0.988-1.000), accuracy was 0.991 (95% CI: 0.978-1.000), sensitivity was 0.969 (95% CI: 0.930-1.000), specificity was 1.000 (95% CI: 1.000-1.000), precision was 1.000 (95% CI: 1.000-1.000), and F1-score was 0.984 (95% CI: 0.964-1.000). The Brier score for the test set was 0.013. Calibration curves and decision-curve analysis demonstrated favourable probability calibration and higher estimated net benefit across a range of threshold probabilities. SHAP-value analysis highlighted that postoperative-day-1 CRP, postoperative-day-3 FIB, postoperative-day-3 APTT, postoperative-day-3 CRP, postoperative-day-3 FDP, postoperative-day-3 PT, postoperative-day-1 UREA, and postoperative-day-1 CREA were major contributing features.

CONCLUSION: The XGBoost model demonstrated excellent discrimination and favorable calibration in the internal test set for identifying postoperative-day-3 ultrasound-detected DVT among patients with FAK. However, several predictors in the final model were measured on postoperative day 3, temporally proximate to the time-point of DVT ascertainment; these biomarkers may reflect biochemical changes secondary to already-formed thrombus rather than pre-thrombotic prospective risk signals. Therefore, the near-perfect discrimination observed in this retrospective cohort should be interpreted cautiously and should not be regarded as definitive evidence of prospective early-prediction performance. Temporal and multicenter external validation using a prespecified prediction time point, ideally restricted to variables available prior to DVT assessment, is required to determine the model's generalizability and prospective clinical applicability.

METHODS: Electronic medical records of 1,071 patients who underwent surgical treatment for FAK at Suining Central Hospital from January 2023 to August 2026 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 749) and a test set (n = 322) at a 7:3 ratio.

articles.title: Cross-elbow stent placement for refractory arteriovenous fistula stenosis and chronic total occlusion in hemodialysis patients: a single-center retrospective cohort of 42 cases.
articles.abstract: Cross-elbow stent placement in hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) has been avoided due to risks of fracture, kinking, deformation, migration, and infection. However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage. Consecutive adult hemodialysis patients who received cross-elbow stents for clinically significant AVF stenosis or CTO (September 2021 - March 2026) at a single center were retrospectively analyzed. Primary outcomes were target lesion primary patency (TLPP), access circuit primary patency (ACPP), access circuit secondary patency, and access circuit assisted primary patency, estimated by Kaplan-Meier. Technical and clinical success and complications were recorded. Forty-two patients were included; 45.2% had CTO and 57.1% had prior PTA. Eluvia-based stents were used in 83.3%. Technical and clinical success were both 100%. Mean access flow increased from 407 ± 267 to 839 ± 188 mL/min. TLPP at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months was 90.1%, 84.4%, 76.9%, and 76.9%, respectively. No stent fracture, migration, kinking, or infection occurred. Cross-elbow stenting was technically feasible and provided favorable short- to mid-term patency without device-related complications, supporting its use as a salvage option for selected refractory AVF lesions and CTOs.
articles.englishSummary: Cross-elbow stent placement in hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) has been avoided due to risks of fracture, kinking, deformation, migration, and infection. However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage.

articles.title: Longitudinal Trends of Intact and Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repairs in the United States: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted access to elective procedures and routine care. Given the risk of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture, understanding repair trends is important to assess the impact of the pandemic on vascular outcomes.

METHODS: This repeated cross-sectional analysis used the TriNetX network, a multicenter US electronic health records database. We included 423 874 patients diagnosed with AAA from 2016 to 2024. Patients were categorized by clinical presentation-intact AAA and ruptured AAA-and stratified by surgical approach: endovascular aneurysm repair or open aneurysm repair. Annual trends in AAA repair rates were assessed using joinpoint regression to calculate annual percentage change.

RESULTS: Among 19 330 AAA repairs, 3791 (19.6%) were open aneurysm repair, and 15 539 (80.4%) were endovascular aneurysm repair. From 2018 to 2024, 1623 repairs (9.9%) were for ruptured AAA and 14 835 (90.1%) were for intact AAA. The rate of intact AAA repairs initially remained stable from 2018 to 2022 but significantly decreased after the pandemic from 2022 to 2024 (annual percentage change, -2.87% [95% CI, -10.95 to -1.00]). In contrast, ruptured AAA repairs rates shifted sharply during the pandemic, with an established prepandemic decline in ruptured repairs from 2018 to 2020 (annual percentage change, -11.48%) reversed, with an increase from 2020 to 2022 (annual percentage change +12.01%), before declining from 2022 to 2024 (annual percentage change, -11.00%).

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, repairs for intact AAA declined, while repairs for ruptured AAA increased during the pandemic period. These trends suggest that potential delays in routine surveillance and elective surgery during the pandemic may have increased acute presentations.
articles.englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted access to elective procedures and routine care. Given the risk of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture, understanding repair trends is important to assess the impact of the pandemic on vascular outcomes. METHODS: This repeated cross-sectional analysis used the TriNetX network, a multicenter US electronic health records database.

articles.title: Training Structure and Satisfaction with Learning in European Vascular Surgery Training: Results from the European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) Surveys.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study describes the availability of modifiable structural training elements across European vascular surgery programmes to identify which of these elements are independently associated with trainees' satisfaction with learning and to contextualise them with trainer reported delivery constraints.

METHODS: The study comprised two parallel cross-sectional web based European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) surveys of trainees and trainers. The main outcome variable was satisfaction with learning (10 point Likert scale). Five modifiable structural elements were identified a priori: structured curriculum; training coordinator; dedicated or protected training time; assigned mentor; and simulation access. Associations were examined using an adjusted linear mixed effects model (LMM), with secondary models for coordinator resourcing and mentorship evaluations. Trainer data were analysed descriptively.

RESULTS: Of 420 trainee responses (32 countries), 273 entered the complete case main LMM. Availability was inconsistent: structured curriculum 56.4%; dedicated or protected training time 34.3%; and simulation access 32.3%. In the adjusted LMM, learning satisfaction was higher with a structured curriculum (= 0.79, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.21 - 1.38; p = .008) and dedicated training time (= 0.62, 95% CI 0.05 - 1.19; p = .035). In secondary models, coordinators with dedicated educational time showed the largest association (= 1.76, 95% CI 1.05 - 2.46; p < .001), and mentorship with regular evaluations was associated with higher satisfaction (= 0.98, 95% CI 0.36 - 1.59; p = .002). Among 659 trainers (37 countries), mentorship importance was rated 8.26 out of 10, yet only 43.4% had dedicated mentorship time; the dominant barrier was clinical workload (84.1%). Desired improvements were dedicated mentorship time (64.4%), formalised programmes (54.3%), and regular feedback sessions (51.6%).

CONCLUSION: A structured curriculum and dedicated training time were independently associated with higher trainee learning satisfaction across European vascular surgery programmes. Organisational roles such as training coordinators and mentors were associated with higher satisfaction in exploratory secondary analyses, suggesting these roles may be most beneficial when actively resourced with dedicated time and regular evaluations. Trainer constraints converged on protected time for training and mentorship.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: This study describes the availability of modifiable structural training elements across European vascular surgery programmes to identify which of these elements are independently associated with trainees' satisfaction with learning and to contextualise them with trainer reported delivery constraints. METHODS: The study comprised two parallel cross-sectional web based European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) surveys of trainees and trainers. The main outcome variable was satisfaction with learning (10 point Likert scale).

articles.title: Prognosis of Patients with Delayed Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Rupture after Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Multicentre Retrospective Study in France.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The majority of patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) undergo endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). Despite its high overall success rate, EVAR does not eliminate the risk of aneurysm rupture. This study aimed to evaluate the prognosis of patients undergoing surgical management for post-EVAR rupture.

METHODS: A multicentre retrospective study of patients who presented with ruptured AAA after successful EVAR between 2007 and 2022 at 22 academic hospitals was conducted. The index EVAR procedures were performed between 2002 and 2020. Data were extracted from electronic hospital records and computed tomography scans. Death during follow up was ascertained using the French register of deceased persons. Survival probabilities at 30, 90, and 365 days were estimated with Kaplan-Meier estimators. Cox proportional hazards survival regression was used to identify determinants associated with increased risk of death.

RESULTS: One hundred and nine patients (96 men) were included, with a mean age of 79.1 ± 9 years at the time of rupture. The median time from index EVAR to rupture was 50 months (range 0 - 179 months). Sixty-seven patients had open surgery (of which 37% underwent suprarenal cross clamping), 39 received endovascular treatment, and three underwent hybrid repair. Overall mortality was 26.6% at thirty days, increasing to 33.9% at ninety days, and 41.3% at 1 year. Neither the type of endoleak nor the type of repair was significantly associated with risk of death during follow up. Post-operative complications were frequent, including renal complications (44.0%), major haemorrhage (22.9%), respiratory distress (19.3%), and mesenteric ischaemia (6%).

CONCLUSION: This study presented a large multicentre series of patients treated for ruptured AAA after EVAR. Despite considerable progress in stent graft technology, EVAR offers little protection in the event of late rupture, even among patients with type II endoleak only. The mortality rate in this study is within the range of those published based on de novo AAA rupture.

Despite its high overall success rate, EVAR does not eliminate the risk of aneurysm rupture. This study aimed to evaluate the prognosis of patients undergoing surgical management for post-EVAR rupture.

articles.title: The Need for Device-Specific Training Before Handheld Ultrasound Use: Agreement and Repeatability of Simulated Aortic Aneurysm Diameter Measurements by Senior Sonography Students on a Familiar Conventional and an Unfamiliar Handheld System.
articles.abstract: Background: Ultrasound measurement of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) diameter guides screening and surveillance, but whether students' measurement competence on a conventional system transfers to an unfamiliar handheld device has rarely been assessed. Methods: Twenty-seven senior sonography students made three anteroposterior outer-to-outer measurements of two water-filled balloons embedded in gelatin (reference diameters 3.53 and 5.88 cm, calculated from the circumference before embedding), first on the familiar cart-based conventional system and then, in a fixed, non-randomised order, on a handheld system with which they had no prior hands-on experience. The primary outcomes were bias against the calculated reference, with equivalence testing (±5%), and the paired between-system difference, with Bland-Altman analysis; repeatability was assessed with repeatability coefficients. Results: Conventional measurements were equivalent to the calculated reference within ±5% (bias -0.09 cm, 95% CI -0.16 to -0.02; +0.07 cm, 95% CI -0.05 to +0.19). Handheld measurements were higher (+0.17 and +0.33 cm; both p < 0.001) and failed equivalence; the mean between-system difference was +0.26 cm (95% CI 0.18-0.34), without proportional bias. Single-reading repeatability coefficients were 0.31-0.67 cm. Conclusions: Students' conventional-system measurements agreed closely with the calculated reference, although this reference was not verified after embedding. Because device type was confounded with operator inexperience and with a fixed testing order, which introduces an unquantifiable learning or fatigue effect, the 0.26 cm value is an observed between-system difference under the study conditions and cannot be attributed to the handheld device itself. Measurement competence did not transfer automatically to a new device, underlining the critical need for device-specific training before handheld systems are used for aortic measurement. These implications are educational and technical; phantom findings do not support clinical surveillance recommendations without confirmation in patients.

articles.title: Predicting Morbidity, Mortality, Revision, and Ambulation in Patients Undergoing Major Lower Limb Amputation for Peripheral Arterial Disease or Diabetes Mellitus: The Case for Regional Level Clinical Prediction Models.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Several outcome prediction tools exist to support decision making for patients undergoing major lower limb amputation (MLLA). However, most predict a single outcome, are derived from registry level data, and lack external validation. The present study aimed to develop clinically focussed, multi-outcome prediction tools using granular regional data with immediate external validation on an international database.

METHODS: This study involved development, and internal and external validation of multivariable binomial and multinomial regression prediction models. All patients undergoing MLLA for ischaemic or diabetic indications between 1 January 2013 and 1 July 2023 at a single regional vascular hub were used for model development. Clinically focussed logistic multivariable binomial and multinomial regression models were developed predicting 30 day and 1 year mortality and revision, 30 day major morbidity or mortality, and best mobility achieved (binary and 3 category). Model complexity, crossvalidated receiver operating curve (ROC) discrimination and calibration were assessed and optimised, with the best performing models undergoing external validation on PERCEIVE study data. External validity was assessed using discrimination and calibration statistics, with one revision attempt permitted.

RESULTS: The development dataset included 609 patients (75.2% men, median age 69 years). Internal crossvalidated ROC values were 0.774 for 30 day mortality, 0.752 for 1 year mortality, 0.679 for 30 day revision, 0.707 for 1 year revision, 0.699 for 30 day major morbidity or mortality, 0.876 for binary best ambulation, and 0.752 for 3 category best ambulation predictions. All models were well calibrated. On external validation the ROC values were 0.616, 0.722, 0.617, 0.488, 0.697, 0.643, and 0.602, respectively.

CONCLUSION: The prediction models performed well for internal "regional" patient outcomes, especially for mortality and ambulation. On external validation, like other models externally validated on the PERCEIVE data, they failed to generalise to the wider population undergoing MLLA, except for 1 year mortality. Predicting patient outcomes from pre-operative variables remains challenging; however, regional level modelling may provide better performance over more general prediction tools.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Several outcome prediction tools exist to support decision making for patients undergoing major lower limb amputation (MLLA). However, most predict a single outcome, are derived from registry level data, and lack external validation. The present study aimed to develop clinically focussed, multi-outcome prediction tools using granular regional data with immediate external validation on an international database.

articles.title: JTH in Clinic: Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) Prophylaxis of Pediatric Patients at Risk of VTE.
articles.abstract: As the incidence of venous thromboembolism (VTE) increases in hospitalized children, there is an urgent need to improve VTE prevention strategies in this population. Implementation of thromboprophylaxis, which includes mechanical and pharmacological interventions, varies in practice due to limited pediatric-specific data and, until recently, a lack of evidence-based guidelines. However, recent randomized clinical trials and well-designed multicenter observational studies have provided improved evidence on the safety and efficacy of anticoagulants for VTE prevention in specific pediatric subpopulations supporting the development of risk assessment models to help identify subgroups of children at high risk for VTE. Based on these data, the American Society of Hematology and International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis recently developed the first evidence-based guideline for anticoagulant prophylaxis in children at risk of VTE. While this guideline is an exciting step towards preventing VTE-associated harm, VTE prevention remains complex due to unique pediatric risk factors and changing physiology with age, resulting in heterogeneous VTE and bleeding risk profiles. In this case-based review, we apply the new guideline and supporting evidence to guide decisions regarding the use of thromboprophylaxis in pediatric cases commonly encountered in clinical practice, highlighting the nuances of VTE prevention in critically ill children. We review the complex decision-making process required prior to initiation of pharmacologic prophylaxis, including assessment of VTE risk, bleeding risk, and shared decision-making with families. Additionally, we highlight the importance of multidisciplinary teams in VTE prevention and anticoagulant stewardship, as well as the similarities and differences in pediatric versus adult practice.

chinaArticles.title: Machine-learning-derived laboratory signatures associated with postoperative day-3 ultrasound-detected lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis after fractures around the knee.
chinaArticles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to construct risk-discrimination models for postoperative-day-3 ultrasound-detected lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) status in patients with fractures around the knee (FAK) using five machine-learning algorithms and compare model performance across five machine-learning algorithms.

METHODS: Electronic medical records of 1,071 patients who underwent surgical treatment for FAK at Suining Central Hospital from January 2023 to August 2026 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 749) and a test set (n = 322) at a 7:3 ratio. Feature selection occurred exclusively within the training dataset. Predictive variables were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, the Boruta algorithm, and recursive feature elimination-extreme gradient boosting (RFE-XGBoost). Five predictive models were developed, including logistic regression, k-nearest neighbor (KNN), random forest (RF), light gradient-boosting machine (LightGBM), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). Model performance was evaluated comprehensively via the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score. Receiver-operating-characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision-curve analysis (DCA) were utilized to identify the selected model. Finally, Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were employed to interpret the global and local prediction outputs of the selected model.

RESULTS: Seventeen overlapping features were identified via feature-selection procedures for final modelling, among which postoperative-day-1 and postoperative-day-3 laboratory biomarkers contributed most substantially to model output. XGBoost was chosen for subsequent SHAP interpretability analyses based on balanced performance observed in cross-validated out-of-fold outputs from the training set. Several non-linear models yielded comparably high discrimination, with overlapping 95% confidence intervals for AUROC.The cross-validated AUC for the XGBoost model in the training set was 0.9932, with a classification threshold of 0.57 derived from the Youden index. In the test set, the AUROC was 0.998 (95% CI: 0.993-1.000), AUPRC was 0.996 (95% CI: 0.988-1.000), accuracy was 0.991 (95% CI: 0.978-1.000), sensitivity was 0.969 (95% CI: 0.930-1.000), specificity was 1.000 (95% CI: 1.000-1.000), precision was 1.000 (95% CI: 1.000-1.000), and F1-score was 0.984 (95% CI: 0.964-1.000). The Brier score for the test set was 0.013. Calibration curves and decision-curve analysis demonstrated favourable probability calibration and higher estimated net benefit across a range of threshold probabilities. SHAP-value analysis highlighted that postoperative-day-1 CRP, postoperative-day-3 FIB, postoperative-day-3 APTT, postoperative-day-3 CRP, postoperative-day-3 FDP, postoperative-day-3 PT, postoperative-day-1 UREA, and postoperative-day-1 CREA were major contributing features.

CONCLUSION: The XGBoost model demonstrated excellent discrimination and favorable calibration in the internal test set for identifying postoperative-day-3 ultrasound-detected DVT among patients with FAK. However, several predictors in the final model were measured on postoperative day 3, temporally proximate to the time-point of DVT ascertainment; these biomarkers may reflect biochemical changes secondary to already-formed thrombus rather than pre-thrombotic prospective risk signals. Therefore, the near-perfect discrimination observed in this retrospective cohort should be interpreted cautiously and should not be regarded as definitive evidence of prospective early-prediction performance. Temporal and multicenter external validation using a prespecified prediction time point, ideally restricted to variables available prior to DVT assessment, is required to determine the model's generalizability and prospective clinical applicability.

chinaArticles.title: Cross-elbow stent placement for refractory arteriovenous fistula stenosis and chronic total occlusion in hemodialysis patients: a single-center retrospective cohort of 42 cases.
chinaArticles.abstract: Cross-elbow stent placement in hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) has been avoided due to risks of fracture, kinking, deformation, migration, and infection. However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage. Consecutive adult hemodialysis patients who received cross-elbow stents for clinically significant AVF stenosis or CTO (September 2021 - March 2026) at a single center were retrospectively analyzed. Primary outcomes were target lesion primary patency (TLPP), access circuit primary patency (ACPP), access circuit secondary patency, and access circuit assisted primary patency, estimated by Kaplan-Meier. Technical and clinical success and complications were recorded. Forty-two patients were included; 45.2% had CTO and 57.1% had prior PTA. Eluvia-based stents were used in 83.3%. Technical and clinical success were both 100%. Mean access flow increased from 407 ± 267 to 839 ± 188 mL/min. TLPP at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months was 90.1%, 84.4%, 76.9%, and 76.9%, respectively. No stent fracture, migration, kinking, or infection occurred. Cross-elbow stenting was technically feasible and provided favorable short- to mid-term patency without device-related complications, supporting its use as a salvage option for selected refractory AVF lesions and CTOs.

articles.title: GRSF1 Ameliorates Neurological Impairment in Cerebral Ischemia/Reperfusion Mice via Regulating Mul1/Mfn2-Mediated Mitochondrial Dynamics and Bioenergetics.
articles.abstract: Guanine-rich RNA sequence binding factor 1 (GRSF1), a mitochondrial RNA-binding protein, plays a critical role in maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis and mitigating oxidative DNA damage. Whether GRSF1 contributes to cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury (CIRI) by regulating mitochondrial dynamics remains to be elucidated. Male C57BL/6 J mice underwent middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) to induce CIRI. Principal component analysis and enrichment analysis were employed to validate impairment in mitochondrial dynamics in CIRI mice. GRSF1 was then evaluated for its effects on neurological function and histology. The role of GRSF1 on mitochondrial dynamics following CIRI was examined through enrichment analysis, electron microscopy, and respiratory chain complex activity assays. The relationship between GRSF1 and mitofusin 2 (Mfn2) in mitochondrial fusion was further investigated. The regulatory mechanism of mitochondrial E3 ubiquitin protein ligase 1 (Mul1) on Mfn2 was assessed using co-immunoprecipitation and denaturing immunoprecipitation assays. CIRI mice were characterized by disrupted mitochondrial dynamics, and restoring this balance ameliorates pathological progression. GRSF1 improved neurological function in CIRI mice, an effect confirmed to associate with maintenance of neuronal mitochondrial dynamics. Mechanistically, GRSF1 promoted mitochondrial fusion by suppressing the expression or activity of Mul1, thereby reducing Mul1-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of Mfn2. Ultimately, GRSF1 attenuated CIRI by inhibiting neuronal mitochondrial dynamic imbalance via the Mul1/Mfn2 pathway. It uncovers GRSF1 as a novel neuroprotective regulator in CIRI and identifies the Mul1/Mfn2 pathway as a critical mechanistic pathway underlying its protective effects. Targeting GRSF1 may hold therapeutic potential by modulating mitochondrial dynamics in CIRI.

articles.title: Disrupting the interaction between T lymphocytes and microglia: Mechanism of Huanglian Jiedu Decoction in the treatment of ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Our previous studies have shown that Huanglian Jiedu Decoction effectively suppresses central immune-inflammatory responses, modulates peripheral inflammatory mediators, reduces the infiltration of peripheral T lymphocytes into the central nervous system, and promotes the conversion of infiltrated T lymphocytes in the brain into Treg cells. However, whether Huanglian Jiedu Decoction can influence M2 microglial polarization by regulating T-lymphocyte phenotypic transformation and thereby modulate neuroinflammation after ischemic stroke remains unclear. This study focused on Treg-mediated microglial polarization to investigate the potential of Huanglian Jiedu Decoction to modulate interactions between T lymphocytes and microglia in the treatment of ischemic stroke. We established a rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion, an inflammatory model of Jurkat T cells stimulated with phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate and ionomycin, and a Transwell co-culture model of T lymphocytes and HMC3 microglia. The results showed that Huanglian Jiedu Decoction effectively alleviated cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in a rat model of middle cerebral artery, inhibited central inflammatory responses, and promoted the polarization of microglia toward the M2 phenotype. Huanglian Jiedu Decoction also promoted the conversion of CD4+ T cells in brain tissue into regulatory T cells and regulated regulatory T cells through the interleukin-10/Janus kinase 1/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 pathway, thereby promoting the activation of M2 microglia. These findings suggest that Huanglian Jiedu Decoction, which has heat-clearing and detoxifying properties, can regulate immune homeostasis, inhibit secondary neuroinflammation associated with ischemic stroke, and exert neuroprotective effects. Huanglian Jiedu Decoction may therefore treat ischemic stroke by modulating the interaction between T lymphocytes and microglia, providing a traditional Chinese medicine-based strategy for the treatment of ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Targeting Fibroblast Foxc2 Promotes Neurovascular Recovery by Suppressing Sdc4 After Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability, with current reperfusion therapies limited by narrow therapeutic windows and inability to promote sustained neurovascular repair. Here, we developed YZD-27, a rationally designed Tanshinone IIA (TSA) derivative with improved druggability, and show that it remains therapeutically effective when administered up to 24 h after ischemic injury in transient and permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO and dMCAO) mouse models. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and cell-cell communication analysis revealed broad cellular responses to YZD-27 and identified fibronectin-1 (Fn1)/syndecan-4 (Sdc4) as a predicted endothelia-fibroblast ligand-receptor interaction. Mechanistically, YZD-27 directly binds forkhead box protein C2 (Foxc2), enhances its protein stability by limiting proteasomal degradation, and increases its occupancy at the Sdc4 promoter, thereby repressing Sdc4 transcription in fibroblast. Fibroblast-conditioned medium experiments further supported a role for Foxc2/Sdc4 regulation in modulating endothelial barrier-related protein expression. These findings identify Foxc2/Sdc4 signaling as a regulatory mechanism associated with the therapeutic effects of YZD-27, and establish YZD-27 as a promising neurovascular therapeutic candidate for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Effects of Exercise Preconditioning on Promoting Endogenous Recovery Responses After Ischemic Stroke in Late-Adult Mice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke causes substantial neurological impairment, and although poststroke rehabilitation can support recovery, neurological deficits often limit the feasibility of exercise in clinical settings. Prestroke exercise has emerged as a potential strategy to enhance resilience to ischemic injury, but most preclinical studies have relied on young adult rodents, in which spontaneous recovery can sometimes obscure clinically meaningful functional effects. However, the impact of exercise preconditioning in later stages of adulthood remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we investigated whether a treadmill exercise preconditioning regimen confers neuroprotection and improves recovery-related responses in late-adult mice subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion.

METHODS: Eight-month-old male mice were assigned to sedentary or exercise groups. Following 5 weeks of treadmill running (5 days per week after 1 week of acclimatization), mice underwent 45 minutes of middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion. Behavioral assessments and body-weight monitoring were performed before and after middle cerebral artery occlusion. Infarct volume and cellular responses were evaluated 14 days after stroke.

RESULTS: Fourteen days after stroke, lesion volume was significantly reduced in the exercise group compared with sedentary controls. Exercise preconditioning enhanced neurogenesis, oligodendrogenesis, and CD31-positive vascular responses while suppressing reactive astrocyte activation. Functional improvements were consistently observed across multiple behavioral assays in late-adult mice.

CONCLUSIONS: Preconditioning with treadmill exercise provides neuroprotection against ischemic stroke in late-adult mice by reducing infarct volume and promoting recovery-associated cellular responses. These findings demonstrate that the functional benefits of prestroke exercise extend beyond the young adult stage and support the potential value of regular physical activity as a strategy to mitigate ischemic brain injury later in adulthood.

articles.title: Atomically dispersed nanoactivators drive innate mitochondrial biogenesis for active neuroprotection in ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Mitigating mitochondrial bioenergetic failure is a pivotal yet formidable neuroprotective goal in treating cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI). However, conventional pharmacological interventions remain largely confined to passive antioxidant defense, which temporarily scavenges reactive oxygen species (ROS) without restoring organelle function. Here, we report a bimetallic nanoactivator (RMV) designed to drive active mitochondrial revival for rescuing ischemic tissues. RMV comprises atomically dispersed ruthenium sites anchored within an oxygen-deficient manganese hydroxide matrix via synergistic Ru-O-Mn bridges. Benefiting from its intrinsic mitochondriotropic properties, RMV effectively intercepts aberrant electron leakage and breaks the self-amplifying cycle of ROS-induced ROS release through cascade multi-enzyme mimetic activities. Importantly, transcriptomic profiling and ultrastructural analysis reveal that RMV transcends passive antioxidant defense by functioning as a bioactive switch. It revives the suppressed SIRT1-PGC1α-TFAM signaling axis, fundamentally driving mitochondrial biogenesis and the reconstruction of functionally intact respiratory chains. In a murine stroke model, RMV treatment induces a 1.52-fold expansion of the neuronal mitochondrial biomass under ischemic stress, thereby suppressing neuronal apoptosis, reducing infarct volumes, and favorably reshaping an M2-polarized neuroimmune microenvironment. These integrated effects yield robust and sustained neurofunctional recovery. Our study shifts the neuroprotective paradigm from reactive damage control to active mitochondrial biogenesis, offering an atomically engineered strategy for ischemic stroke management.

articles.title: Stage-Associated Efficacy of Systemically Administered Neural Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes in Ischemic Stroke through the Prevention of Cx43 Degradation.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke pathology is highly dynamic, making the optimal timing for biological interventions highly elusive. This study investigated the stage-associated therapeutic efficacy of neural stem cell-derived exosomes (NSC-Exos) for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion. The in vivo evaluations identified a restricted therapeutic window closely associated with the temporal evolution of the ischemic microenvironment. Early exosome intervention (4 or 24 h post-ischemia) significantly reduced infarct volume, restored blood-brain barrier integrity, and improved neurological functional recovery. In contrast, delayed administration (48 h) failed to reduce the mortality rate and provide meaningful neuroprotection. To examine the molecular basis of this time dependence, we integrated temporal proteomic profiling of the ischemic penumbra with small RNA sequencing of NSC-Exos. The analytical and functional data suggest that early NSC-Exo delivery transfers miR-9-5p to suppress Nedd4 expression, thereby restoring the Connexin 43 protein pool and stabilizing the astrocytic network to halt initial microenvironmental collapse. Collectively, this study underscores the critical importance of intervention timing and provides a potential translational strategy for utilizing NSC-Exos as a targeted, stage-specific therapy in acute ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Neutrophil-hitchhiking and microglia-homing liposomes co-delivering artemisinin and edaravone for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury treatment.
articles.abstract: Clinical outcomes of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) remain unsatisfactory, largely because the blood-brain barrier (BBB) restricts the delivery of most neuroprotective agents to the brain parenchyma. Although artemisinin (ART) and edaravone (EDV) have shown promising therapeutic potential for CIRI, their clinical application is hindered by their short in vivo half-lives and poor aqueous solubility. Neutrophil infiltration triggered by CIRI provides a unique opportunity for drug delivery across the BBB, whereas targeted modulation of microglia represents a key strategy for mitigating reperfusion-induced injury. However, existing neutrophil hitchhiking delivery systems primarily focus on BBB traversal and generally lack a secondary targeting mechanism to promote preferential drug accumulation within the inflammatory core of the ischemic brain. Here, we developed a dual-modified liposomal system functionalized with sialic acid (SA) and phosphatidylserine (PS) (ART/EDV-PS/SAL) for the co-delivery of ART and EDV. This system enables sequential two-step targeting through SA-mediated neutrophil hitchhiking for BBB traversal, followed by PS-mediated microglial homing within ischemic brain tissue. In a mouse model of CIRI, ART/EDV-PS/SAL markedly reduced cerebral infarct volume, preserved BBB integrity, and significantly improved neurological and behavioral outcomes. Mechanistically, ART/EDV-PS/SAL exerted neuroprotective effects by suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation, attenuating pyroptosis, and promoting microglial polarization toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. By harnessing endogenous immune cells to achieve efficient and sequential drug targeting, this study establishes a promising nanodelivery platform for the treatment of ischemic stroke and other neuroinflammatory disorders.

articles.title: Thrombus stiffness depends on occlusion site and influences thrombectomy outcomes in acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Only 60% of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) achieve successful reperfusion after the first endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) attempt. In vitro studies have shown that thrombus stiffness influences thrombus-device interaction and retrieval efficacy. This prospective observational study investigates how thrombus stiffness relates to clinical factors, thrombus imaging characteristics and histological composition. It further explores the association between thrombus stiffness and EVT success, as measured by the modified first-pass reperfusion (mFPR).

PATIENTS AND METHODS: A total of 281 thrombus samples were collected from 51 AIS patients undergoing EVT. Thrombus stiffness was quantified using compressive mechanical testing, composition from histological staining and radiological characteristics from pre-interventional non-contrast computed tomography (CT) and CT angiography. Statistical analysis was performed using linear and logistic mixed-effects regression models.

RESULTS: Thrombi retrieved from the proximal M2 segment of the middle cerebral artery showed significant lower stiffness (0.236 kPa, 95% CI, 0.136-0.409) compared to those from the M1 segment (0.760 kPa, 95% CI, 0.492-1.174) and from the ICA (1.106 kPa, 95% CI, 0.558-2.192). Occlusion location was the strongest clinical marker of thrombus stiffness. Adjusted mFPR probability was 40.4% (95% CI, 24.5-67.0) for thrombi retrieved from the ICA, 89.7% (95% CI, 79.5-97.0) for M1 occlusions, and 53.0% (95% CI, 30.8-84.7) for M2 occlusions.

CONCLUSION: Thrombi in distal vessels of the anterior cerebral circulation are significantly softer than those in proximal intracranial arteries. First-pass EVT success is lower for the stiffest thrombi from the ICA and for the softest thrombi from M2, providing a foundation for future biomechanically informed thrombus removal strategies to optimise AIS treatment.

articles.title: Remote ischemic preconditioning protects against cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury through lactate-dependent AMPK/ULK1 signaling and autophagy.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury is a major contributor to ischemic cerebral damage and poor functional outcomes following ischemic stroke, and effective neuroprotective strategies remain limited. Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) has emerged as a promising, noninvasive approach; however, its underlying mechanisms are incompletely understood. Here, we investigated whether lactate serves as a key metabolic mediator linking RIPC to neuroprotection through regulation of autophagy. Using an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model in PC12 cells and a middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model in rats, we demonstrate that I/R impairs autophagic flux, as evidenced by p62 accumulation and reduced LC3-II and Beclin-1 expression, leading to increased cellular apoptosis and injury. Lactate supplementation restored autophagic flux, enhanced cell viability, and suppressed apoptosis under OGD/R conditions. Mechanistically, lactate activated the AMPK/ULK1 signaling pathway, whereas pharmacological inhibition of AMPK or ULK1 attenuated lactate-induced autophagy and cytoprotection. In vivo, RIPC elevated plasma and cerebral lactate levels, activated AMPK/ULK1 signaling, promoted autophagy, reduced infarct volume, and improved acute neurological outcomes. Notably, blockade of lactate transport or inhibition of AMPK/ULK1 signaling attenuated these protective effects. Collectively, our findings suggest that lactate serves as an important mediator of RIPC-induced neuroprotection and reveal a novel lactate-AMPK/ULK1-autophagy axis that mitigates cerebral I/R injury. These results provide mechanistic insight into RIPC and suggest potential therapeutic targets for ischemic stroke.
